newsitem.title: PERU: Lima bolsa ends stable as market quietens.
newsitem.headline: Lima bolsa ends stable as market quietens.

text.p: The Lima Stock Exchange closed broadly stable on Monday as the market settled down after a recent bull run and consequent profit-taking, brokers said.
They predicted another quiet session Tuesday, with investor enthusiasm for the mining sector probably bringing some gains.
According to preliminary figures, the bolsa's General Index rose 0.05 percent Monday to 2,127.44 points while the blue-chip Selective Index was flat at 3,073.32.
"The market closed stable with a reasonable volume after the profit-taking of last week," said Jaime Jera, of Inversion y Desarrollo brokerage.
Trade totalled 26.5 milion soles ($10 million) on 1,626 operations.

Polymetallic miner Atacocha gained 5.0 percent to 2.52 percent on world zinc prices, and an anticipated share dividend. Another miner Perubar closed up 0.95 percent to 6.40 soles, while benchmark Telefonica del Peru rose 1.46 percent to 6.93 soles.
Among losers, miner Morococha fell 1.56 percent to 6.32 soles, while electric utilities Edelnor and Edegel lost 1.42 percent to 2.09 soles and 1.40 percent to 1.41 soles respectively.
Overall, 39 stocks fell, 27 rose and 25 were flat.
Carlos Guimeth, of Multivalores brokerage, said while most stocks had reached their equilibrium after recent gains, the industrial sector still looked set to expand.

"The economic improvement makes us think that industrial companies could register interesting results from the third quarter," he said, specifically recommending brewery group Union de Cervecerias Backus and Aceros Arequipa.
